title: Pilot weekly sync — onboarding runbook & env ownership
meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-04 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Samira, Jonah (Redwood) — Maya, Ethan, Priya (PortBridge)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on onboarding runbook alignment, access ownership for VPC/gateway creds, quick review of benchmark spikes (tail latency), and next steps for security docs and a runbook sign-off. Decided to proceed with dedicated staging cluster for 2-week focused latency runs. Several action items assigned.
transcript:
[00:00] Samira Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Well do a quick 40-ish minute sync — runbook alignment, who owns what creds, and a short review of the benchmarks from last night. Jonah and I will cover the infra pieces, Maya/Ethan/Priya you can jump in.
[00:18] Maya Ortega: Perfect, thanks. We pulled the nightly perf summary earlier but wanted to hear your read on that p95 spike.
[00:27] Jonah Li: Yeah so quick context — we saw a p95 token latency bump on the 11PM run, it correlates with longer sequence lengths in the test set and one of your tests used batch size 16 which caused a KV cache miss pattern.
[00:39] Ethan Shaw: Right — we have an internal job that replays long sessions to simulate user flows, might be the culprit.
[00:45] Samira Patel: Good to know. For the runbook, we want to make ownership explicit: PortBridge to own account-level VPC peering and firewall rules, Redwood to own API gateway keys and canary routing config. Does that mapping work for you?
[01:02] Priya Menon: We need to confirm where logs are stored — audit logs must live in our splunk instance per compliance. Can Redwood forward post-processed traces?
[01:14] Jonah Li: Yes, we can send traces to your collector via the VPC egress; we support both syslog and HTTP ingest. Well need a collector endpoint and a short-lived token for the handoff.
[01:26] Maya Ortega: Also, on credential rotation: Ethan asked that we use KMS-wrapped keys on your side. Any blockers?
[01:33] Jonah Li: Not blockers, just an integration step. Well provide the KMS key policy example in the runbook.
[01:40] Samira Patel: I shared a draft runbook in the invite notes — link: https://redwood.internal/pilot-runbook-v2.pdf. Please comment inline before Friday so we can finalize ownership boundaries.
[01:53] Ethan Shaw: Quick question on the dedicated vs hosted discussion — in the last meeting you recommended a small dedicated staging pool to reproduce the spike. Can you explain the tradeoffs again?
[02:03] Jonah Li: Sure — dedicated staging gives you deterministic GPU locality and no noisy neighbors, so tail latency is reproducible. Hosted is cheaper but sampling variability makes debugging harder. For a two-week targeted latency validation we typically recommend dedicated staging with the same quant profiles and autoscale settings youll use in prod.
[02:20] Maya Ortega: Cost is a concern; can we limit the dedicated pool to night windows only?
[02:25] Samira Patel: Absolutely, you can schedule reserved capacity to spin up for 8–10 hours per night during the validation window to keep costs down. Well include an estimate in the follow-up.
[02:36] Priya Menon: On the security checklist — we need SOC2 documentation, RBAC matrix, and proof of encryption-in-transit keys. I think you sent a SOC one pager last month, can we get the full pack?
[02:49] Samira Patel: Yes, well share the SOC2 bundle and RBAC export. Ill assign that to Jonah to deliver to Priya.
[02:57] Jonah Li: On it. I also want to call out one infra note: the test runner that created the long sequences was from your replay cluster and it spikes the KV cache because it touches many different conversation IDs; a small change to the replay to reuse conversation prefixes reduces the miss rate significantly.
[03:12] Ethan Shaw: Oh — we can tweak that. That might be the low-lift fix.
[03:16] Maya Ortega: Could you show the specific diff?
[03:19] Jonah Li: Ill attach a sample patch in the runbook repo after the call.
[03:24] [03:24] Samira Patel: Okay moving on to access — we still need the VPC CIDR ranges from PortBridge and the collector endpoints for logs, plus an initial API key to validate routes. Who owns sharing those?
[03:36] Maya Ortega: Ethan can send the CIDR ranges and the collector endpoint later today.
[03:40] Ethan Shaw: Yes Ill send them by end of day, and Ill create a jira for the replay change.
[03:46] Priya Menon: For the API key wed like keys with scoped IP allowlists; can Redwood support per-key IP restrictions?
[03:54] Jonah Li: Yes, we support per-key allowlists and also per-route RBAC. Well document the steps in the runbook.
[04:03] Maya Ortega: On benchmarks — the nightly CSV shows p50 at 42ms, p95 at 420ms, and a small number of outliers up to 900ms. What were the sequence lengths for those outliers?
[04:15] Jonah Li: The 900ms hit came from sequences ~2.5k tokens, which are rare in production but your replay included them. The model switches to a slower attention kernel beyond 2k tokens which accounts for the jump.
[04:29] Ethan Shaw: So tuning quant profiles will not help that kernel change?
[04:33] Jonah Li: It helps a bit — quant/packing reduces absolute time per token but the algorithmic change for long sequences dominates. For those cases we recommend either a soft truncate or a long-sequence optimized variant of the model.
[04:45] Samira Patel: For the pilot, we propose the following: 1) reproduce spike in dedicated staging using the replay tweak, 2) test with both soft-truncation and the optimized variant, 3) collect traces to your Splunk instance for root cause. Does that sound actionable?
[04:59] Maya Ortega: Yes, thats clear. Well need a decision point after the dedicated staging runs — whether to accept soft truncation or adopt the optimized model.
[05:07] Samira Patel: Correct — and well flag that decision in the runbook with acceptance criteria (p95 under 300ms for target traffic and less than 2% outliers).
[05:18] Priya Menon: One more security item: audit log format needs a cryptographic checksum for tamper detection. Can the logs include a per-batch HMAC?
[05:27] Jonah Li: We can add an HMAC header to the log bundle before its forwarded; well confirm algorithm and key handling with your security team.
[05:35] Ethan Shaw: Great. On the infra ownership: who will run the canary cutover if we do A/B?
[05:40] Samira Patel: Redwood can orchestrate the canary and rollback; PortBridge should own the CD pipeline triggers. Well provide the webhook details for auto rollback if latency SLOs breach.
[05:51] Maya Ortega: Sounds good. Anything else on the runbook?
[05:54] Jonah Li: Ill add a small appendix that documents the KV cache warmup pattern and recommended batch sizes per sequence length bucket. Small change: for sequences >1k tokens we recommend batch size 4 instead of 8 to lower memory churn.
[06:08] Maya Ortega: Ok well try that.
[06:11] Samira Patel: Wrapping up — recap and next steps. Ill read the agreed items then we can confirm.
[06:16] Samira Patel: Recap: Ethan sends CIDRs + collector endpoint by EOD, Jonah posts replay patch and appendix, Redwood shares SOC2 bundle and RBAC export, PortBridge to spin up dedicated staging for two-week window nights-only, runbook comments due Friday, decision gate after staged runs on truncation vs optimized model.
[06:35] Ethan Shaw: Confirmed — Ill also open the jira for the replay tweak and tag Jonah.
[06:40] Priya Menon: Ill review the SOC2 docs and send any follow-up questions.
[06:44] Maya Ortega: And Ill schedule the dedicated staging start date in the pilot calendar for next Monday night, pending cost estimate.
[06:51] Samira Patel: Perfect. Thanks everyone, well share the follow-up email with links and action items in the next hour.
[06:58] Jonah Li: Thanks all.
[07:00] Meeting ends (approx)
